correctness.rationale: Normalize projective coordinate triples over F₃ by first nonzero coefficient 1; obtain 13 points and 13 lines, each line containing 4 points. The 26-vertex bipartite *nonincidence* graph has nine neighbors per vertex. Its open Lovász neighborhood complex splits into disjoint point and line components, and duality identifies each with all nonempty subsets of 13 nine-point line complements. I independently constructed every one of 3,861 faces and confirmed dimension-ordered f-vector (13,78,286,702,1170,1014,468,117,13). Independent F₂ reduced boundary ranks (1,12,66,220,482,649,364,104,13), with first entry augmented ∂0, yield β4=39, β5=1. More importantly, I independently reconstructed the package's pivot toggle matching: 1,910 nonempty-face pairs and exactly 1 critical vertex, 39 critical 4-cells and 1 critical 5-cell; the full 20,085-edge oriented Hasse diagram topologically sorts (no directed cycle). An independent signed integral Morse reduction computes all 39 components of the unique critical 5-cell boundary to be zero. The 4-skeleton is a wedge of 39 S4, for which π4≅H4 by Hurewicz; zero attaching degrees imply the 5-cell is null-attached. Thus each component ≃(∨39 S4)∨S5, without mistaking mod-two homology for an integral homotopy proof.
